title: Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act

claims.claim: Requires Small Business Administration employees who help originate, review, or approve SBA loans to certify
claims.sourceSpan: personally and substantially participate in the origination,
claims.note: 'help originate, review, or approve' maps to 'personally and substantially participate in the origination, review, or approval of a loan administered by the Administration'; 'help' softens 'personally and substantially participate' but is directionally faithful.

claims.claim: must first certify in writing
claims.note: 'prior to such participation ... certify to the Administrator in writing' — 'first' = prior to participation; 'in writing' verbatim on the next line.

claims.claim: that they have no prohibited conflict of interest in the loan

claims.note: 'does not have any conflict of interest prohibited under section 208 of title 18 ... or section 2635.502 of title 5 ... with respect to such participation in such loan'.

claims.sourceSpan: recuse themselves from participating in such loan
claims.note: 'upon learning of any such conflict of interest after submitting such certification, will immediately disclose ... and recuse themselves' — later-discovered conflict triggers recusal. Polarity correct (recuse, not continue).

claims.note: 'an employee of the Administration that will ... participate in the ... loan shall ... certify to the Administrator in writing'.

claims.claim: The implementing regulations are due before the certification duty begins
claims.note: Objective arithmetic from two source figures: regs due at 180 days (Sec. 2(b)) precede the certification effective date at 270 days (Sec. 2(a)).

claims.claim: The bill requires a written no-conflict certification but does not specify a penalty for an employee who files a false certification beyond existing conflict-of-interest law
claims.sourceSpan: the Administrator shall issue regulations implementing this
claims.note: Accurate provable-absence: Sec. 2 creates the certification duty and a regulations mandate but contains no penalty clause; the only referenced consequences are the pre-existing 18 U.S.C. 208 / 5 C.F.R. 2635.502 regimes.

claims.claim: The certification applies to employees who "personally and substantially participate" but the bill does not define that threshold
claims.note: 'personally and substantially participate' is verbatim in Sec. 2(a); the Sec. 2(c) definitions block defines only 'Administration' and 'Administrator', not the participation threshold. Provable absence.

claims.claim: New written conflict-of-interest certification requirement for SBA employees involved in loans, effective 270 days after enactment
claims.note: New duty created by Sec. 2(a) ('shall ... certify ... in writing'); effective '270 days after the date of the enactment'.

claims.claim: Coverage check: every material source provision (short title; Sec. 2(a) certification duty effective at 270 days; the three certification contents — no COI under 18 U.S.C. 208 / 5 C.F.R. 2635.502, immediate disclosure + recusal of later-discovered conflicts, understanding of applicable requirements; Sec. 2(b) regulations within 180 days; Sec. 2(c) definitions) is represented in the analysis; nothing material omitted or buried
claims.note: Two-section bill; the analysis captures both sections plus the staggered 180-day/270-day ordering (underreported) and two genuine gaps (no false-certification penalty; undefined participation threshold). No material provision dropped. featured_quotes/criticisms are Congressional Record floor statements not present in the bill-text source and were not audited here (out of scope for source-only fidelity).

notes: Simple two-section integrity bill (Introduced-in-House text; versionChanges reports unchanged through Engrossed). Every figure (270 days, 180 days), statutory cite (18 U.S.C. 208, 5 C.F.R. 2635.502), the sponsor/cosponsor count, and the short title match the source verbatim. Direction correct throughout (new mandatory certification duty, recusal on later-discovered conflict — no polarity inversion). No material issues; 0 omissions.
